item.text:
<linkedin_post>Indonesia’s Ministry of Health is fine-tuning two Google models on domestic chest X-rays as part of its tuberculosis screening plans. Running the models on local infrastructure would allow patient data to remain within the country.

The ministry aims to screen 50 million people a year, a volume that would be difficult to review manually. MedSigLIP can be adapted to classify medical images, while MedGemma can work with images and clinical text.

Local control also brings responsibility for testing how well the models perform on the patients and equipment they will encounter. A screening result can help identify someone who needs further testing; it does not confirm a TB diagnosis.</linkedin_post>
